blueprint_topic: Management of Care — appropriate collaboration with a nonclinical birth-support professional
stem: A laboring client has a doula in addition to the RN and obstetric clinician. Which action by the RN best reflects appropriate collaboration with the doula?

options.A: Invite the doula to continue comfort measures and help the client communicate preferences while the RN performs clinical assessments and treatments.
options.B: Invite the doula to interpret the fetal heart-rate tracing and recommend whether the RN should notify the obstetric clinician about possible intervention.
options.C: Ask the doula to select and administer one of the client's prescribed as-needed analgesics while the RN completes care for another client.
options.D: Rely on the doula to communicate the client's preferences during care discussions without confirming those preferences directly with the client.

rationale: A is correct. CMS defines doula services as emotional, physical, and informational support provided by a nonclinical trained professional and specifically includes physical comfort measures, information, emotional support, advocacy, and active participation on the birth team during labor and delivery. ACOG likewise recommends respectful teams that include doulas and describes doulas as facilitating communication between clinicians and patients while providing continuous support. B is incorrect because interpreting a fetal heart-rate tracing and deciding whether clinical escalation or obstetric intervention is indicated requires clinical assessment and judgment, which is incompatible with the cited nonclinical doula role. C is incorrect because selecting and administering a prescribed analgesic is clinical medication management, not one of the nonclinical doula support functions described by CMS. D is incorrect because ACOG advises that when a doula communicates on behalf of a patient, clinicians should acknowledge the doula and verify the communication directly with the patient; doula advocacy supports, but does not replace, the client's own confirmation of preferences.
educational_objective: Collaborate with a doula as a nonclinical member of the birth team by preserving appropriate comfort, informational, advocacy, and communication support while the RN retains responsibility for clinical assessment, treatment, medication management, and direct confirmation of the client's preferences.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists (ACOG); Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
source_document_title: Partnering With Doulas in Clinical Settings, Committee Statement No. 31; Transforming Maternal Health (TMaH) Model Frequently Asked Questions
source_version_date: ACOG Committee Statement No. 31, August 2026, published online July 16, 2026; CMS TMaH FAQ current page accessed 2026-08-20
source_locator: ACOG Committee Statement No. 31 — Summary of Recommendations and Conclusions: create synergistic, respectful teams that include doulas. Background/Recommendations and Conclusions: doulas provide support and facilitate communication between clinicians and patients. Box 2, Strategies to Foster Open and Positive Communication: when doulas communicate on behalf of a patient, acknowledge the doula and ask for verification from the patient. CMS TMaH FAQ — Model Elements, Question 20, 'What doula care services will be covered in the TMaH Model?': doula services are emotional, physical, and informational support provided by a nonclinical trained professional; Labor and Delivery includes physical comfort measures, information, emotional support, advocating for beneficiary needs, and being an active member of the birth team.
source_claim_supported: A doula is a nonclinical birth-team support professional whose appropriate role includes physical comfort, informational and emotional support, advocacy, and communication support; collaboration should complement rather than replace clinical nursing assessment, treatment, medication management, or direct confirmation of the client's preferences.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, page 7: 'Advocate for client rights and needs'; 'Identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members when providing client care'; 'Recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources'; 'Provide care within the legal scope of practice.'

correction_summary: Rebuilt distractors to remove the absolute-word cue, reduce answer-length cueing, eliminate cartoonishly implausible alternatives, and keep all options within the same collaboration/scope construct. Correct answer and core clinical concept retained.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly supported by CMS labor-and-delivery doula functions and ACOG clinician-doula collaboration guidance.
option_audit.B: Plausible role-boundary distractor; wrong because it assigns clinical fetal-monitor interpretation and escalation judgment to a nonclinical doula.
option_audit.C: Plausible workload/scope distractor; wrong because it assigns medication selection and administration to a nonclinical doula.
option_audit.D: Plausible advocacy/communication distractor; wrong because ACOG specifically requires verification with the patient when the doula communicates on the patient's behalf.
